question: Which force arises when a body is immersed in a fluid and displaces the fluid?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Buoyant Force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Buoyant force is the upward force exerted by a fluid that opposes the weight of an object immersed in it.
 
• This force arises because the fluid displaced by the object creates a pressure difference between the top and bottom of the object.
 
• Buoyant force is governed by Archimedes' principle, which states that the upward force is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.
 
• It plays a crucial role in enabling objects like ships to float on water and balloons to rise in the air.
 
• Buoyant force depends on the density of the fluid and the volume of the object submerged.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Archimedes' Principle:**

 
 
• Discovered by the Greek mathematician Archimedes, this principle explains buoyancy.
 
• It states that a body submerged in a fluid experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.
 
 
 
• **Density and Buoyancy:**
 
 
• An object floats if its density is less than the density of the fluid it is immersed in.
 
• Objects denser than the fluid sink due to insufficient buoyant force to counter their weight.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Buoyant Force:**
 
 
• Used in designing ships, submarines, and floating devices.
 
• Helps in understanding the functioning of hot air balloons and hydrometers.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Buoyant Force:**
 
 
• The volume of the object submerged: Larger volume displaces more fluid, increasing buoyant force.
 
• The density of the fluid: Higher density fluids exert greater buoyant force.
